title: SWIGH-SCORE: A lightweight approach for detecting rearranged immunoglobulin heavy chains
author: Hansen, Maagaard, et al.

steps.title: Set up analysis environment
steps.instruction: Prepare a Linux system (Ubuntu 18‑22 LTS or similar) with gcc and awk installed; run the analysis either on a local 24‑core workstation (e.g., Intel i9‑9920X) or on the UCloud interactive HPC system.

steps.title: Isolate CD138+ cells
steps.instruction: Isolate CD138‑positive plasma cells from a diagnostic bone‑marrow sample using StraightFrom Whole Blood CD138 microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec, Bergisch Gladbach, Germany) on an AutoMACS separator (Miltenyi Biotec).

steps.title: Extract DNA and make low‑level dilutions
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the isolated CD138+ cells. Dilute the DNA into a pool of leukocyte DNA obtained from 13 control donor samples to achieve 10⁻⁴–10⁻⁵ dilutions (1:10,000 to 1:100,000). Low‑level detection replicates will be sequenced only on the Ion GeneStudio S5 System.

steps.title: Generate IGH FR1 amplicons
steps.instruction: Amplify the immunoglobulin heavy‑chain rearranged region from each DNA preparation using the LymphoTrack IGH FR1 Assay (Invivoscribe, San Diego, CA).

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction:
Prepare libraries for each sequencing platform:
- Illumina MiSeq: follow the standard LymphoTrack library protocol.
- Ion GeneStudio S5: use the IGH FR1 amplicons directly.
- Oxford Nanopore MinION Mk1C: pool the Illumina MiSeq amplicon DNA library and construct a library with the Ligation Sequencing Kit (SQK‑LSK110) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Perform deep sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the baseline specimen on all three platforms, targeting 0.2–1.6 million reads per run (median read lengths: 301 bp MiSeq, 317 bp Ion S5, 476 bp MinION). For pseudo‑MRD assessment, run serial dilutions (10⁻⁴ and 10⁻⁵) on the Ion S5: 1 replicate for the 10⁻⁴ dilution and 5 replicates for the 10⁻⁵ dilution, obtaining 1.8–2.6 million reads per run.

steps.title: Quality‑filter FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Run the provided C program `quality-filter` on each FASTQ file. Retain reads longer than 200 bp and with mean Phred quality ≥ Q20 (error rate ≤ 1 %). The program processes ~1 million reads in 7–8 seconds and uses <200 MB RAM.

steps.title: Download IMGT reference sequences
steps.instruction: Download immunoglobulin heavy‑chain V and J germ‑line reference sequences from IMGT/GENE‑DB via the IMGT/V‑Quest website (accessed 20 April 2023) and make them available to the analysis pipeline.

steps.title: Run swigh‑clonotype‑amplicon
steps.instruction: Execute `swigh-clonotype-amplicon` (single‑process) on the filtered reads. Expect 73.5–83.2 % match to IGHV3‑11×06 and 80.6–87 % match to IGHJ4×02, with runtimes of 9–70 seconds depending on read count.

steps.title: Run swigh‑clonotype‑random
steps.instruction: Execute `swigh-clonotype-random` (default 1000 reads, 63 processes) on the filtered reads. The tool should assign the correct clonotype in 49–63 seconds.

steps.title: Run swigh‑score at 98 % similarity
steps.instruction: Run `swigh-score` (multiprocess Smith‑Waterman) with a 98 % sequence‑similarity threshold on all reads (63 processes). Record clonal fractions: 0.44 for Ion S5, 0.85 for MiSeq, and runtime ≈1–3 minutes per million reads.

steps.title: Filter reads by similarity thresholds
steps.instruction: If the Ion S5 clonal fraction appears low, filter out reads with similarity <25 % before re‑running `swigh-score`. For Nanopore data, set the similarity threshold between 90 % and 85 % (reflecting ~10 % error rate) to obtain clonal fractions of 0.77–0.97.

steps.title: Prepare pseudo‑MRD samples
steps.instruction: Create one 10⁻⁴ dilution and five 10⁻⁵ dilutions of the diagnostic DNA. Spike each sample with a control sequence equivalent to 100 cells. Sequence these samples on the Ion S5, obtaining up to 2.6 million reads per replicate (processing time ≈324.8 s on a 24‑core workstation, ≈321.1 s on the HPC).

steps.title: Calculate clonal fractions and absolute burden
steps.instruction: For the pseudo‑MRD samples, compute clonal fractions at the 98 % similarity threshold (expected 38 × 10⁻⁴ for the 10⁻⁴ dilution and 56 × 10⁻⁵ for the 10⁻⁵ dilution). Using the 100‑cell spike‑in, convert to absolute malignant cell counts: 6.4 malignant cells per 100 000 leukocytes for the 10⁻⁴ dilution and 50.9 per 100 000 for the 10⁻⁵ dilution.
